text:
Max Sasson keeps finding the net on a Canucks team that can't find wins. He has 6 goals in 21 games, the latest a redirect in Edmonton on Nov 7, on about 12 and a half minutes a night, and he has done it as an undrafted free agent who came up through Abbotsford.

Two things are going on, and they pull in opposite directions. His own finishing is running hot: 6 goals on 2.84 expected goals (the quality of his chances), a 24% shooting rate that rarely lasts. But with him on the ice, Vancouver has scored 12.7 fewer goals than its chances deserved, which is why he has just one assist. That usually swings back. In between, the process is good: the Canucks have 49.3% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, 12 points better than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 57% of his entries last season, and carry-ins led to a chance far more often than dump-ins. What we'd watch is his ice time, 9.8 minutes against the Rangers on Friday.
headline: Sasson keeps scoring for a team that keeps losing
